title.en: Short answers, so do I / neither do I, and question tags
title.es: Respuestas cortas, so do I / neither do I y question tags

summary.en: In short answers, English repeats the auxiliary from the question: _Yes, I **do**._ _No, she **isn't**._ To agree, use **so + auxiliary + subject** after a positive statement and **neither / nor + auxiliary + subject** after a negative one. To avoid repeating a clause, use _I think **so**_, _I hope **so**_ or _I hope **not**_. **Question tags** (_isn't it?_, _did they?_) ask for confirmation: a positive statement takes a negative tag and a negative statement takes a positive one.
summary.es: No basta con «sí» o «no»: en inglés se repite el auxiliar (Yes, I do). «Yo también» es So do I y «yo tampoco» es Neither do I, con el verbo antes del sujeto. Los question tags equivalen a «¿verdad?» o «¿no?», pero cambian según el auxiliar.

form: Short answer: **Yes/No** + subject + auxiliary (_Yes, I did._ _No, he hasn't._)
Agreeing: **So** + auxiliary + subject (_So do I_); **Neither / Nor** + auxiliary + subject (_Neither can she_)
Replacing a clause: **I think / hope / expect / suppose / am afraid + so**; negative: **I don't think so**, **I hope not**, **I'm afraid not**
Question tag: statement + auxiliary + pronoun with opposite polarity (_You've met, haven't you?_)
No auxiliary in the statement → **do / does / did**; **I am** → **aren't I**; **Let's** → **shall we**; imperatives → **will you**

uses.text: **Short answers** repeat the auxiliary of the question: _'Were you at the meeting?' 'No, I wasn't.'_ Use _do / does / did_ when the question uses the present or past simple.
**Agreeing**: _'I love hiking.' 'So do I.'_ _'I haven't got a car.' 'Neither have I.'_ To disagree, stress the auxiliary: _'I'm not tired.' 'Well, I am!'_
**Think so, hope not**: _'Is the shop open on Sundays?' 'I don't think so.'_ _'Will prices go up again?' 'I'm afraid so.'_ _'Will the exam be hard?' 'I hope not.'_
**Tags** with a falling voice ask the listener to confirm; with a rising voice they are real questions: _You're a teacher, aren't you?_ _He doesn't smoke, does he?_

note.en: If the voice goes down, you expect agreement. If it goes up, you really don't know.
note.es: Si la voz baja, esperas que te den la razón. Si sube, de verdad preguntas.

uses.text: **Special cases**: _I'm late, **aren't I**?_ _Let's start, **shall we**?_ _Open the window, **will you**?_ _Nobody called, **did they**?_ _There's a problem, **isn't there**?_

note.en: Nobody, nothing, never and hardly make a statement negative, so the tag is positive.
note.es: Nobody, nothing, never y hardly ya son negativos, así que el tag va en positivo.

why.en: After so and neither the auxiliary comes before the subject.
why.es: Después de neither y so se invierte el orden: auxiliar + sujeto.

mistakes.wrong: You don't like fish, don't you?
mistakes.right: You don't like fish, do you?

why.en: A negative statement takes a positive tag.
why.es: Si la frase es negativa, el tag es afirmativo.

why.en: A short answer repeats the auxiliary, not the main verb.
why.es: Se responde con el auxiliar de la pregunta, no con el verbo principal.

why.en: After think, hope and expect we use so, not yes.
why.es: No existe «I think yes»: se dice I think so.

examples.en: 'Did you get my message?' 'Yes, I did, thanks.'
'I've never been to Japan.' 'Neither have I.'
examples.es: —No he estado nunca en Japón. —Yo tampoco.

examples.en: 'I'd love a day off.' 'So would I.'
examples.es: —Me encantaría tener un día libre. —A mí también.

examples.en: 'Is Sam coming tonight?' 'I think so, but I'm not sure.'
'Will the exam be hard?' 'I hope not.'
She doesn't work on Sundays, does she?
Nobody has told them, have they?
I'm in the right room, aren't I?

explanation.en: The statement is negative, so the tag is positive and repeats the auxiliary have.
To agree with a positive statement we use So + auxiliary + subject.

practice.prompt: 'I can't swim very well.' '___ can I.'

explanation.en: To agree with a negative statement we use Neither + auxiliary + subject.

practice.prompt: 'Is the shop open on Sundays?' 'I don't think ___.'

explanation.en: I don't think so is the usual short negative answer.
The tag after Let's is shall we.
The tag for I am is aren't I.
